summary: Join our training course on nutrition and food security in rural areas. Learn effective strategies to improve health and well-being in underserved communities.
lede: Nutrition and food security training helps rural program professionals assess food insecurity and the drivers of malnutrition. It covers identifying vulnerable groups, using basic dietary and household assessment tools, and selecting nutrition-sensitive or nutrition-specific interventions for needs such as seasonal hunger and shocks. Participants also explore links with health, water, sanitation and social protection, track outcomes with suitable indicators, and communicate findings and program limitations.
audienceIntro: This course is specifically designed for professionals who need to integrate nutrition and food security into their work, ensuring tangible improvements in rural communities.
audience: Agribusiness and value chain actors interested
modules: Foundations of Nutrition and Food Security in Rural Areas
Understanding Rural Vulnerability and Who Is at Risk
Drivers of Malnutrition in Rural Communities
Food Systems and Diet Quality in Rural Contexts
Assessment Tools for Nutrition and Food Security Programming
Nutrition-Specific Approaches and When to Use Them
WASH, Health, and Social Protection Links to Nutrition
Climate, Resilience, and Food Security Risk Management
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning for Nutrition and Food Security
Community Engagement, Communication, and Behavior Change
Building Proposals and Reporting Results to Stakeholders
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of rural development challenges and some experience in program management or implementation.
